title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第4章
content_zh:
第4章 办公室里的硝烟

    周一早上八点半，我站在顾氏大厦楼下，手里拎着一杯便利店的美式咖啡，抬头看了一眼二十七楼的窗户。

    窗帘拉着。顾西辞已经到了。

    我的手机震了一下。是他发来的消息，五个字：直接上顶楼。

    顶楼是二十七楼。上次我去的是他的办公室，这次他让我去的是同层的会议室。我进了电梯，按下二十七，电梯镜面里映出一个穿黑色西装裙的女人。今天没穿阿玛尼，换了一套上周在商城买的国产品牌，剪裁不错，面料一般，但胜在是自己的钱买的。脚上是一双五厘米的黑色高跟鞋，高度适中，站一天不会太累。我对着镜子整了一下领口，把嘴角往上提了提。

    电梯门开了。

    二十七楼的走廊很长，铺着深灰色的地毯，两侧的办公室门都关着，只有尽头的会议室大门敞开着，里面隐约传来说话声。我走到门口的时候，脚步顿了一下。

    会议室里不止顾西辞一个人。

    长条会议桌的左侧坐着两个我没见过的男人，一个四十岁左右，戴金丝眼镜，面前摊着一沓文件，看起来像是财务或者法务。另一个更年轻，三十出头，穿着深蓝色的西装，手里拿着一支笔，在记事本上飞快地写着什么。顾西辞坐在会议桌的主位上，面前摆着一杯黑咖啡，衬衫领口的扣子松了一颗，袖子卷到手肘，看起来已经工作了一段时间。

    “进来。”他头也不抬。

    我走进会议室，在他右手边的位置坐下。这个位置是他用眼神示意我坐的——不是正对面，不是隔壁，是右手边隔了一个空位的距离。既不算太亲近，也不算太疏远。一个很精准的距离。

    “这位是温小姐，我的合约搭档。”顾西辞对着那两个人介绍我的时候用的是“合约搭档”四个字，不是“合约伙伴”，更不是“合约金丝雀”。然后他转向我，“这位是法务部的陈律，这位是财务部的郑主管。”

    陈律推了推眼镜，朝我点了点头，目光在我脸上停留了两秒。郑主管抬头看了我一眼，笑了一下，那笑容很职业，但眼睛里带着一点不易察觉的打量。他们都知道我是谁。热搜挂了三天，这座大厦里恐怕没有人不知道。

    “今天叫你来，是因为万盛那边出了点状况。”顾西辞把一份文件推到我面前，“许向平上周六晚上，也就是高尔夫打完之后的当天晚上，给我们的并购案合作方发了邮件。邮件里暗示顾氏的现金流有问题，建议对方重新评估合作风险。”

    我翻开文件。是那封邮件的打印件，内容不算长，措辞很讲究，从头到尾没有一句明确的指控，全是“建议关注”“审慎评估”“可能存在的不确定性”这样的措辞。这种邮件在法律上告不了他，但在商场上足以让合作方起疑心。

    “许向平不是跟你在球场上称兄道弟吗？转头就捅刀子？”

    “不叫捅刀子。叫试探。”顾西辞靠在椅背上，手指在桌面轻轻敲了两下，“他昨天输了三杆，面子挂不住。加上陈鹤东在球场上的态度有所松动，他感觉到了威胁。所以他想在合作方那边制造一点不确定因素，给我增加压力。”

    “那现在合作方什么反应？”

    “对方暂时没有回复，但也没按原计划推进合同。”法务部的陈律接过话，语气沉稳，“按流程，本周五之前应该走完尽调程序。如果周五没有完成，项目可能会延期至少一个月。”

    “延期一个月会有什么后果？”

    郑主管翻开面前的报表，报了一串数字。具体金额我不方便在此复述，但那是一个足以让任何公司感到压力的数字。现金流一旦紧张，后续跟银行和其他合作方的谈判都会受影响。

    会议室里安静了几秒。空调出风口发出轻微的嗡嗡声。

    “我能做什么？”我问。

    顾西辞转头看我，眼神里多了一点我说不清楚的东西。不是怀疑，不是期待，是介于两者之间的某种试探。

    “今天下午两点，许向平的太太林曼如办了一个茶会。名义上是茶会，实际上是替她老公探口风。被邀请的人里，有你。”

    “有我？林曼如办的茶会为什么会邀请我？”

    “因为你是这个圈子里的新变数。你的出现打乱了所有人的预期。他们以为假千金会灰溜溜地消失，结果你不仅没消失，还在林氏晚宴和青城球场上连续两次抢了风头。”他从文件夹里抽出一张请柬推到我面前，浅粉色的卡片，烫金的字，写着“春日下午茶雅集”，地点在林家的私宅，“许向平一定会让她太太来试探你。你的态度，在某种程度上会被他们解读成我的态度。他们现在还不确定你对我有多重要，所以想通过你来估算我的底线。”

    我把请柬拿起来，正面反面看了一遍。林家的私宅在城东的别墅区，开车过去大概四十分钟。

    “你希望我传达什么态度？”

    “你很稳。”他说，“你不在乎许向平的小动作，因为你觉得那些小动作伤不到顾氏的根本。你不在乎，就代表我不在乎。”

    “好。那如果她们问我球场上输给你的感受呢？”

    “这种问题不会有人当面问。”

    “如果问了呢？”

    他顿了顿，嘴角浮起一点弧度：“那你就说，输给我是应该的。”

    我从会议室出来，先去了一趟洗手间。镜子里的人看起来还算镇定，但手心又湿了。我抽了一张纸巾擦手，把下午要做的事在脑子里过了一遍。茶会，林曼如，许向平的探子。她们会用最温柔的语气问最刁钻的问题，会用最好的茶点招待最被看不起的人。我的任务不是反击，而是让她们摸不透。

    阿May接到我的电话的时候正在棚里给一个网红做造型，背景音里能听到吹风机的声音。

    “温大小姐，怎么想起给我打电话了？”

    “江湖救急。下午有个茶会，富太太局，林曼如的场子。我现在需要一份装备，不能太隆重，不能太随便，不能让人觉得我在讨好，也不能让人觉得我在挑衅。”

    “要求这么多，你怎么不自己变出一套来？”

    “我衣柜里只有三套能穿的衣服，两套你见过，一套是运动服。”

    电话那头传来她叹气的声音：“你怎么混的，好歹也是热搜名人了，连件像样的衣服都买不起？”

    “钱要花在刀刃上。”

    “刀刃是什么？”

    “注册公司的启动资金。”

    她沉默了一秒，然后说：“你过来吧。我这儿有一套香奈儿的早春系列，米白色，刚到的新款。你要是穿着效果好，算我赞助的。”

    “赞助？”

    “对，以后你发达了给我当活广告。”

    四十分钟后我到了阿May的工作室。她正蹲在地上给那个网红缝裙边，嘴里叼着两根别针，看见我进来，站起来把别针从嘴里取下来，上下打量了我一眼。
content_en:
Chapter 4 Smoke in the Office
At 8:30 on Monday morning, I stood downstairs in Gu's Building, holding a cup of American coffee from a convenience store in my hand, and looked up at the window on the 27th floor.
The curtains were drawn. Gu Xici has arrived.
My phone vibrated. It was a message from him, five words: Go directly to the top floor.
The top floor is the twenty-seventh floor. Last time I went to his office, this time he asked me to go to the conference room on the same floor. I entered the elevator and pressed twenty-seven. A woman in a black suit and skirt was reflected in the elevator mirror. I didn't wear Armani today. I changed into a domestic brand that I bought in the mall last week. The cut is good and the fabric is average, but the advantage is that I bought it with my own money. On her feet are a pair of five-centimeter black high-heeled shoes with a moderate height, so she won't be too tired after standing all day. I adjusted my neckline in front of the mirror and raised the corners of my mouth.
The elevator door opens.
The corridor on the twenty-seventh floor is very long, covered with dark gray carpets. The office doors on both sides are closed. Only the door of the conference room at the end is open, and faint voices can be heard inside. When I walked to the door, I paused.
Gu Xici was not the only one in the conference room.
Sitting on the left side of the long conference table were two men I had never seen before. One was about forty years old and wore gold-rimmed glasses. He had a stack of documents spread out in front of him. He looked like he was in finance or legal affairs. The other was younger, in his early thirties, wearing a dark blue suit, holding a pen in his hand and writing something quickly on a notepad. Gu Xici was sitting at the head of the conference table, with a cup of black coffee in front of him. One button on the collar of his shirt was loose, and his sleeves were rolled up to his elbows. He looked like he had been working for a while.
"Come in." He didn't even look up.
I walked into the conference room and sat down on his right side. He motioned me to sit in this seat with his eyes - not directly opposite, not next door, but with an empty seat to the right. Neither too close nor too distant. A very precise distance.
"This is Miss Wen, my contract partner." When Gu Xici introduced me to the two people, he used the word "contract partner", not "contract partner", let alone "contract canary." Then he turned to me, "This is Chen Lu from the Legal Department, and this is Director Zheng from the Finance Department."
Chen Lu pushed up his glasses, nodded towards me, and his eyes stayed on my face for two seconds. Manager Zheng looked up at me and smiled. The smile was very professional, but there was an unnoticeable look in his eyes. They all know who I am. It has been on the hot search list for three days, and I’m afraid no one in this building doesn’t know about it.
"I called you here today because something happened at Wansheng." Gu Xici pushed a document in front of me. "Xu Xiangping sent an email to our M&A partner last Saturday night, the night after golf. The email suggested that Gu's cash flow was problematic and suggested that the other party re-evaluate the risks of cooperation."
I opened the file. It was a printout of that email. The content was not long and the wording was very particular. There was no clear accusation from beginning to end. It was all wordings like "suggested attention", "prudent assessment" and "possible uncertainties". This kind of email cannot sue him legally, but it is enough to make the partners suspicious in the business.
"Didn't Xu Xiangping become brothers with you on the court? Then he turned around and stabbed you?"
"It's not called stabbing. It's called testing." Gu Xici leaned back in his chair and tapped his fingers on the table twice. "He lost three shots yesterday and couldn't lose face. In addition, Chen Hedong's attitude on the court has loosened, and he felt threatened. So he wanted to create some uncertainty on the partner's side and put more pressure on me."
"What is the reaction of the partners now?"
"The other party has not responded yet, but it has not advanced the contract as originally planned." Chen Lu from the Legal Department took over with a calm tone, "According to the process, the due diligence process should be completed before this Friday. If it is not completed by Friday, the project may be delayed by at least a month."
"What will be the consequences of a one-month delay?"
Manager Zheng opened the report in front of him and reported a series of figures. I’m not comfortable repeating the exact amount here, but it’s a figure that’s enough to put any company under pressure. Once cash flow is tight, subsequent negotiations with banks and other partners will be affected.
The conference room was quiet for a few seconds. There was a slight buzzing sound coming from the air conditioner vents.
"What can I do?" I asked.
Gu Xici turned to look at me, there was something in his eyes that I couldn't explain clearly. It's not doubt, it's not expectation, it's some kind of temptation in between.
"At two o'clock this afternoon, Xu Xiangping's wife Lin Manru held a tea party. It was a tea party in name, but in fact it was to talk to her husband. One of the people invited was you."
"With me? Why did Lin Manru invite me to the tea party held by Lin Manru?"
"Because you are a new variable in this circle. Your appearance disrupted everyone's expectations. They thought that the fake daughter would disappear in despair, but not only did you not disappear, you also stole the spotlight twice in a row at Lin's dinner and Qingcheng Stadium." He pulled out an invitation from the folder and pushed it in front of me, a light pink card. The film, with gilded characters, reads "Spring Afternoon Tea Gathering", and the location is the private residence of the Lin family. "Xu Xiangping will definitely ask his wife to test you. Your attitude will be interpreted by them as mine to a certain extent. They are not yet sure how important you are to me, so they want to use you to estimate my bottom line."
I picked up the invitation and read it front and back. The Lin family's private residence is in the villa area in the east of the city. It takes about forty minutes to drive there.
"What attitude do you want me to convey?"
"You are very stable." He said, "You don't care about Xu Xiangping's little moves, because you think those little moves can't hurt the foundation of the Gu family. If you don't care, it means I don't care."
"Okay. What if they ask me how it feels to lose to you on the court?"
"No one would ask this question face to face."
"What if I asked?"
He paused, and the corner of his mouth curved a little: "Then just say that you deserve to lose to me."
I came out of the conference room and went to the bathroom first. The person in the mirror looked calm, but his palms were wet again. I took out a tissue to wipe my hands and went over in my mind what I had to do in the afternoon. Tea party, Lin Manru, Xu Xiangping's spy. They will ask the most difficult questions in the gentlest tone, and treat the most looked-down people with the best refreshments. My task is not to fight back, but to keep them guessing.
When May received my call, she was styling an internet celebrity in the studio, and the sound of a hair dryer could be heard in the background.
"Miss Wen, why did you remember to call me?"
"Jianghu is in urgent need. There is a tea party in the afternoon, at the Rich Lady Bureau, at Lin Manru's place. I need a piece of equipment now. It can't be too grand, it can't be too casual, and it can't make people think that I'm trying to please or provoke."
"There are so many demands, why don't you come up with something yourself?"
"I only have three wearable outfits in my wardrobe, two you've seen, and one is a sportswear."
Her sighing voice came from the other end of the phone: "How do you manage to become a popular celebrity and not even be able to afford decent clothes?"
"Money needs to be spent wisely."
"What's the blade?"
"Start-up capital for registered companies."
She was silent for a second, and then said: "Come here. I have a set of Chanel's early spring series here, off-white, a new model that has just arrived. If you wear it well, I will sponsor it."
"sponsor?"
"Yes, you will be a living advertisement for me when you get rich."
Forty minutes later I arrived at May’s studio. She was squatting on the ground sewing the skirt of that Internet celebrity, holding two safety pins in her mouth. When she saw me coming in, she stood up, took the safety pins out of her mouth, and looked me up and down.
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 4
